_meta.purpose: Published real-world figures for SLATE's life simulation: pickup trucks (A), recreational boats and light aircraft (B), car-wrap removal and partial wraps (C), Mexico City LP gas and SACMEX water (D), utility outages (E), and vehicle crime by where the car is parked (F). Markets: US, UK, Ireland, Canada, Mexico.
_meta.conventions: confirmed = true only where the figure was read on the publisher's own page or PDF during retrieval (HTML fetched directly, or a PDF/XLSX downloaded from the publisher and converted to text locally). confirmed = false where the figure came from a search-engine excerpt, a press report of the publisher's figure, or a page that could not be loaded; the note says which. Figures are never estimated or derived here, except where a note shows the plain arithmetic.
_meta.accessNotes: ford.com, ford.ca, ramtrucks.com, chevrolet.com and toyota.com refused the summarising fetcher (HTTP 403) but served full HTML to a direct request; prices were read from those pages' own markup. gob.mx (CNE) returned a JavaScript challenge page, so no CNE figure could be read at the source.

US_California.rule: California charges a weight fee on commercial vehicles, explicitly including pickups, based on unladen weight and axles, in addition to other registration fees. "A weight fee based on the vehicle's unladen weight and number of axles is imposed on commercial vehicles (trucks, pickups, and some trailers)." "Weight fees for pickup trucks and electric vehicles are calculated under this section."
US_California.effective: 01/01/2002 (VC §9400) for vehicles with declared GVW of 10,000 lb or less

source.title: Vehicle Industry Registration Procedures Manual — Appendix 1F Fees

US_California.example: A 2026 F-150 at the 4,391 lb minimum curb weight falls in band D ($80); a 5,710 lb Silverado falls in band E ($154). Curb weight is used here as a stand-in for DMV unladen weight, which can differ slightly.

EnglandWales_CSEW.definition: Note 10: "'Semi-private' includes outside areas on the premises and garages or car parks around but not connected to the home." So a driveway is semi-private; 'Private' is the home's own private area (its exact definition is in the CSEW user guide, not this workbook).

source.title: Nature of crime: vehicle-related theft, year ending March 2025 (Tables 2a–2c)

EnglandWales_CSEW.caution: These are shares of incidents by location, not risk per car parked there. Turning them into a per-location theft risk needs the share of cars normally parked in each place, which this table does not give. The theft-of-vehicle base is small (103 incidents), so single-year shares move a lot.
